tools.title: Gable & Rake Wall Stud Calculator
tools.desc: Length of every stud beneath a sloping top plate
tools.formula: height(x) = start + x × pitch/12; cut = height − plate deduction
tools.example: 144 in wall, 96 in start height, 6:12 gives end height 168 in before plates
tools.limit: Geometry only; no structural approval

tools.title: Wall Framing with Doors & Windows
tools.desc: Plot full-height studs and reference king/jack centers around up to three door or window openings, each with its own sill and height.
tools.formula: Use OC grid outside opening side packs; jack centers = opening edges ± studWidth/2; king centers = edges ± 1.5×studWidth; rough opening top = sill + height.
tools.example: 120 in wall, 16 in OC, 1.5 in studs, opening from 32 to 68 in, 80 in high: six unaffected grid centers and four opening-side reference centers.
tools.limit: Reference geometry only: opening elevations are not precut member lengths. Headers, cripples, sill framing, plate deductions, structural sizing and code compliance require separate design.

guidance.heading: Door and window elevations share a floor datum
guidance.text: Set sill to 0 for a door. For a window, enter its sill elevation and opening height separately. The cutout shows the rough opening only; headers, cripple studs and trim are not generated.

guidance.heading: Jack and king positions are center marks
guidance.text: Each jack and king reference center is calculated from a clear opening edge and the stud width. Regular on-center members inside these side packs are omitted. Verify actual stock, rough-opening tolerances, and local requirements before cutting.

tools.title: Deck Board & Gap Calculator
tools.desc: Number of straight decking rows and last rip width
tools.example: 120 in at 5.5 in board + 0.125 in gap gives 22 rows and 1.875 in final rip
tools.limit: No joist load design or joint optimization

tools.title: Baluster & Spindle Spacing
tools.desc: Equal clear gaps and individual baluster coordinates
tools.example: 96 in clear, 1.5 in faces, 4 in maximum: 17 balusters, 3.9167 in gaps
tools.limit: Not a safety-code compliance certificate

tools.title: Common Rafter & Birdsmouth Reference
tools.desc: Ridge-adjusted rafter line, overhang and birdsmouth seat-notch depth reference
tools.example: 120 in run at 6:12 yields rise 60 in and reference line 134.164 in
tools.limit: Seat length is a horizontal cut-reference, not a certified birdsmouth or heel. Notch thickness is measured normal to the rafter's long edges; stock grade, bearing width, local code and roof loads must be checked independently. Diagram is a schematic, never a 1:1 saw template.

guidance.heading: Measure the run and ridge reference
guidance.text: Measure the horizontal run to the ridge centerline, then enter the actual ridge board thickness. The tool subtracts half that thickness before computing the bearing-to-ridge line length. Roof pitch is the vertical rise over 12 inches of horizontal run, not the angle of the saw blade.

guidance.heading: Differentiate seat length and notch depth
guidance.text: The seat input is a horizontal projection along the bearing line. The vertical rise across that span is seat × pitch/12. The depth of that wedge measured perpendicular to the long rafter edges is seat × sin(arctan(pitch/12)). It is NOT the same as the full rafter stock depth or a bearing-capacity verification.

guidance.heading: Check the support and eave separately
guidance.text: The wall bearing point and overhang tail are listed separately in the measurement schedule. The line from ridge to bearing excludes the eave extension; the total slope distance includes it. Ridge-to-bearing and ridge-to-eave dimensions use the same pitch but must not be confused.

guidance.heading: Do not cut from this SVG at paper scale
guidance.text: Confirm the actual plumb/seat layout using a framing square and reference faces on scrap lumber. Ridge connection, roof loads, seat bearing, notch limits and local requirements are outside this geometry model. The diagram is deliberately not a certified full-size template.

tools.title: Crown Molding Compound Cuts
tools.desc: Compound miter and bevel angles with hand and corner options
tools.example: 38° spring and 90° corner: miter ≈31.62°, bevel ≈33.86°
tools.limit: Saw conventions vary; cut a scrap sample

tools.title: Soffit Drop & Eave Section
tools.desc: Roof-line drop over a stated horizontal eave projection
tools.formula: reference drop = projection×pitch/12; adjusted datum = drop+named offsets
tools.example: 24 in horizontal eave at 6:12: nominal drop 12 in
tools.limit: Datum and offset signs require on-site confirmation

tools.title: Kerf Bending Layout
tools.desc: Trial kerf spacing for a requested curve
tools.example: 100 mm radius and 90° arc: 157.08 mm arc length
tools.limit: Empirical springback and wood grain are not predicted

tools.title: Wainscoting Panel Layout
tools.desc: Equally sized panels between margins and gaps
tools.example: 120 in wall, 5 panels, 3 in margins, 2 in gaps: 21.2 in panels
tools.limit: Doors, skirting and stile dimensions excluded

tools.title: Straight Stair Calculator
tools.desc: Riser count, rise, tread count and run
tools.example: 105 in / 7.5 in ⇒ 14 risers and 13 treads
tools.limit: Geometry, not a stair-code certificate

tools.title: Rise & Run Slope Converter
tools.desc: Rise/run, slope angle and hypotenuse
tools.limit: Run must be nonzero

tools.title: Deck Material Estimator
tools.desc: Decking board and simple joist layout quantities
tools.formula: area=width×length; board rows from board width and gaps; layout joists at chosen OC
tools.example: 10 × 12 ft footprint = 120 ft² before waste
tools.limit: Framing positions are not safe joist spans

tools.title: Segmented Bowl Ring Calculator
tools.desc: Ring segment chords and wedge cutting angles
tools.formula: half miter=180/n; outer chord=Douter×sin(π/n); inner chord=Dinner×sin(π/n)
tools.example: Twelve segments require 15° end miter
tools.limit: Finished sizes exclude cutting stock and kerf

tools.title: Roof Pitch in Degrees & Percent
tools.desc: Convert 12-inch roof pitch to angles and rise
tools.limit: Roof geometry only

tools.title: Equal Center Spacing
tools.desc: Place points exactly between two end offsets
tools.example: 1000 mm and 6 endpoint centers ⇒ 200 mm intervals
tools.limit: Offsets are to centers, not item edges

tools.title: Hip Rafter Line Geometry
tools.desc: Plan diagonal, roof rise and three-dimensional hip line
tools.example: 120 by 120 in plan and 6:12 rise gives plan 169.706 in
tools.limit: No load or compound-cut structural sizing

tools.title: Hip Roof Sheet Layout Calculator
tools.desc: Divide an equal-pitch rectangular hip roof into four actual slope-face panels, inspect clipped sheet layouts and export cut coordinates.
tools.formula: Slope factor = sqrt(1+(pitch/12)^2). Each hip plane becomes a local triangle or trapezoid. Clip its outline to every sheet rectangle and sum the resulting polygon areas.
tools.example: For a flat 192 × 96 in hip-roof footprint and 96 × 48 in sheets, area requires at least four sheets, but a separate-sheet-per-cut layout uses six positions.
tools.limit: Geometry of an equal-pitch rectangular four-plane roof only. Sheets are placed in straight eave-origin rows, without seam gaps, staggering, offcut reuse, fastening or building-code checks. Plans are scaled schematics and NOT certified full-size cutting templates.

guidance.heading: Sheet orientation and the four local axes
guidance.text: The default places the long sheet edge parallel to each roof eave and the short edge up the slope. Rotate by 90 degrees with the sheet direction control. The (eave, uphill) coordinates in the table restart at each of the four roof planes.

guidance.heading: Cut polygon coordinates
guidance.text: For each listed sheet, cut vertices are measured from that sheet's lower-left local corner. The colored rooftop plan view projects exactly those clipped polygons into a bird's-eye diagram. The CSV preserves all row coordinates for bench-side checking.

guidance.heading: No offcut reuse or engineered joint layout
guidance.text: A cut sheet may contain a small triangular remnant that this conservative count discards. This is not optimized stock nesting, a structural sheathing schedule, or a substitute for checking fastening, edge setbacks and actual cut tolerances.

tools.title: Wall Stud Count & Layout
tools.desc: Regular vertical stud centers and last-end placement
tools.formula: positions=0, OC multiples below L, and exactly one far end
tools.example: 120 in at 16 in spacing gives 9 locations
tools.limit: Opening studs require dedicated framing tool

tools.title: Shelf Spacing & Drill Marks
tools.desc: Even clear shelves inside a case opening
tools.example: 1000 mm interior, three 20 mm shelves ⇒ 235 mm clear gaps
tools.limit: Shelf strength not assessed

tools.title: Gable Roof Area Calculator
tools.desc: Two planar roof areas using width, pitch and overhangs
tools.example: A symmetric gable has two matching roof planes
tools.limit: Dormers, valleys and waste excluded

tools.title: Square Layout Diagonal Checker
tools.desc: Ideal diagonal and deviations from measured diagonals
tools.example: 3×4 ft rectangle has 5 ft ideal diagonal
tools.limit: Equal diagonals alone do not prove squareness

tools.title: Diagonal Brace Calculator
tools.desc: Brace diagonal centerline and angle
tools.example: 3 ft × 4 ft ⇒ 5 ft brace reference
tools.limit: No end joinery or load calculation

tools.title: Hole Spacing Drilling Guide
tools.desc: Drilling centers, pitch and hole fit checks
tools.example: 100 mm board, 4 holes, 5 mm center offsets: 30 mm pitch
tools.limit: Holes must fit and not overlap

tools.title: Straight Stair Stringer Cut Reference
tools.desc: Straight stair stringer stepped cut coordinates, bottom rise correction and nominal remaining throat
tools.example: 105 in / 14 risers => 7.5 in rise and 13 treads of 10 in; with 1.5 in tread material, bottom cut rise is 6 in if lower finished floor is already installed
tools.limit: Reference for conventional straight stair stringer layout only. Total rise MUST be finished-floor to finished-floor. Lower finish is additional floor thickness laid after the stringer is installed (set 0 if existing). Top connection, nosing, minimum throat, fasteners and structural capacity require field verification. Do not overcut corners; SVG is not a 1:1 cutting template.

guidance.heading: Use finished-floor to finished-floor total rise
guidance.text: Measure the total rise between the final finished elevations of the lower and upper floors. Under this conventional layout, the upper floor functions as the last walking surface, so a staircase with 14 risers has 13 separate wooden treads. Alternative flush-top and hanger arrangements are not modeled.

guidance.heading: Lay out a repeatable tread/riser step
guidance.text: Each vertical riser is total rise ÷ number of risers. The first riser has horizontal position zero; each next riser is one tread run farther along. The table lists the horizontal reference and upper elevation of every riser, including the top-landing vertical.

guidance.heading: Correct the bottom cut for installed finishes
guidance.text: For the conventional bottom cut, subtract the finished tread thickness from one nominal riser height. Add only the lower finished-floor layer that will be installed AFTER the stringer is set. If you measured to an already completed lower finished floor, enter zero for this additional layer.

guidance.heading: Understand the throat estimate
guidance.text: Normal penetration of a step notch into the board is (riser × tread run) ÷ √(riser² + tread run²). The nominal remaining throat is board depth minus that perpendicular notch penetration. This is not an engineering rating; minimum stock size, bearing, attachments, nosing and code compliance must be checked on the actual installation.

tools.title: Roof Sheathing Calculator
tools.desc: Rectangular single-plane sheathing layout with true sloped depth, clipped edge sheets and a complete cut schedule
tools.formula: True sloped depth = roof plan width × sqrt(1+(pitch/12)^2); clip a grid of stock sheets to the roof plane; purchase count = occupied sheet positions plus optional allowance.
tools.example: A flat 110 × 70 in roof plane with 96 × 48 in sheets needs four sheet positions, including three edge cuts, before allowance.
tools.limit: Single rectangular roof plane only; eave-origin grid without seam gaps, staggering, offcut reuse, fastening, bearing or structural compliance checks. SVG is a scaled schematic, not a certified 1:1 pattern.

guidance.heading: Understand eave and uphill dimensions
guidance.text: Roof plan width measures the horizontal uphill run; plan length measures the eave. The pitched run is converted to its true sloped surface length before positioning each sheet.

guidance.heading: Review every sheet cut
guidance.text: The diagram shows the single plane in flat sloped-surface coordinates. Eave start and slope start locate each sheet from the lower-left eave corner. Cut along and cut uphill are the cut dimensions, all exported in CSV.

guidance.heading: Conservative purchasing, not a fastening plan
guidance.text: Every occupied position consumes one stock sheet without offcut reuse. Compare sheet orientations to reduce the conservative count. Allowance applies to occupied sheets, not the area lower bound; confirm real fastening, seam and support details separately.
